ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Two parallel lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ lie on a plane, distance $d$ apart. On $\ell_1$ there are an infinite number of points $A_1, A_2, A_3, ...$ , in that order, with $A_nA_{n+1} = 2$ for all $n$. On $\ell_2$ there are an infinite number of points $B_1, B_2, B_3,...$ , in that order and in the same direction, satisfying $B_nB_{n+1} = 1$ for all $n$. Given that $A_1B_1$ is perpendicular to both $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$, express the sum $\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \angle A_iB_iA_{i+1}$ in terms of $d$.\n<image1>

Points \(A_1,A_2,A_3,\ldots\) are on the upper straight line, and points \(B_1,B_2,B_3,\ldots\) are on the lower straight line. In the figure, \(A_1\) is directly above \(B_1\), and \(A_1B_1\) is perpendicular to the two parallel lines. Each marked angle is located at \(B_i\), formed by the rays \(B_iA_i\) and \(B_iA_{i+1}\). Establish a coordinate system according to the figure: let the lower straight line be the \(x\)-axis, and take \(B_1=(0,0)\). Since \(B_nB_{n+1}=1\), \(B_i=(i-1,0)\). The distance between the two lines is \(d\), and \(A_1\) is directly above \(B_1\), so \(A_1=(0,d)\). Also, since \(A_nA_{n+1}=2\), \(A_i=(2(i-1),d)\). Viewed from \(B_i=(i-1,0)\), \(\overrightarrow{B_iA_i}=(i-1,d)\), and \(\overrightarrow{B_iA_{i+1}}=(i+1,d)\). Let \(f(k)=\arctan(d/k)\), and define \(f(0)=\pi/2\). Then the angle that ray \(B_iA_i\) makes with the positive horizontal direction is \(f(i-1)\), and the angle that ray \(B_iA_{i+1}\) makes with the positive horizontal direction is \(f(i+1)\). Therefore \[ \angle A_iB_iA_{i+1}=f(i-1)-f(i+1). \] Summing the first \(N\) terms: \[ \sum_{i=1}^N \angle A_iB_iA_{i+1} =\sum_{i=1}^N [f(i-1)-f(i+1)] =f(0)+f(1)-f(N)-f(N+1). \] When \(N\to\infty\), \(f(N),f(N+1)\to 0\), so the total sum is \[ f(0)+f(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan(d). \] Since \(d>0\), there is \[ \arctan(d)+\arctan(1/d)=\frac{\pi}{2}, \] so \[ \frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan(d)=\pi-\arctan(1/d). \] Therefore the desired sum is \(\pi-\tan^{-1}(1/d)\).

图像描述：图中有两条水平的平行直线，上方直线是 \(\ell_1\)，下方直线是 \(\ell_2\)。点 \(A_1,A_2,A_3,\ldots\) 在上方直线上，点 \(B_1,B_2,B_3,\ldots\) 在下方直线上。图中 \(A_1\) 正在 \(B_1\) 上方，\(A_1B_1\) 垂直于两条平行线。每个标出的角位于 \(B_i\) 处，由射线 \(B_iA_i\) 和 \(B_iA_{i+1}\) 夹成。

按图建立坐标系：令下方直线为 \(x\)-轴，取 \(B_1=(0,0)\)，因为 \(B_nB_{n+1}=1\)，所以 \(B_i=(i-1,0)\)。两条线距离为 \(d\)，且 \(A_1\) 在 \(B_1\) 正上方，所以 \(A_1=(0,d)\)。又因为 \(A_nA_{n+1}=2\)，所以 \(A_i=(2(i-1),d)\)。

从 \(B_i=(i-1,0)\) 看，\(\overrightarrow{B_iA_i}=(i-1,d)\)，\(\overrightarrow{B_iA_{i+1}}=(i+1,d)\)。令 \(f(k)=\arctan(d/k)\)，并定义 \(f(0)=\pi/2\)。那么射线 \(B_iA_i\) 与水平正方向的夹角是 \(f(i-1)\)，射线 \(B_iA_{i+1}\) 与水平正方向的夹角是 \(f(i+1)\)。因此
\[
\angle A_iB_iA_{i+1}=f(i-1)-f(i+1).
\]

对前 \(N\) 项求和：
\[
\sum_{i=1}^N \angle A_iB_iA_{i+1}
=\sum_{i=1}^N [f(i-1)-f(i+1)]
=f(0)+f(1)-f(N)-f(N+1).
\]
当 \(N\to\infty\) 时，\(f(N),f(N+1)\to 0\)，所以总和为
\[
f(0)+f(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan(d).
\]
因为 \(d>0\)，有
\[
\arctan(d)+\arctan(1/d)=\frac{\pi}{2},
\]
所以
\[
\frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan(d)=\pi-\arctan(1/d).
\]
因此所求和为 \(\pi-\tan^{-1}(1/d)\)。

图像描述：图中有两条水平平行直线，上方直线上标有 A1,A2,A3,A4,A5，下方直线上标有 B1,B2,B3,B4,B5。A1 在 B1 的正上方，A1B1 是竖直线段；从每个 Bi 画出了到 Ai 和 A_{i+1} 的斜线段，因此图中每个要求的角就是在 Bi 处由射线 BiAi 与 BiA_{i+1} 形成的角。

推理：按方法取坐标 B_i=(i-1,0)，A_i=(2i-2,d)，其中 d 是两平行线距离。于是从 B_i 指向 A_i 的向量为 A_i-B_i=(i-1,d)，用复数表示为 z_i=(i-1)+i d；从 B_i 指向 A_{i+1} 的向量为 A_{i+1}-B_i=(i+1,d)，用复数表示为 w_i=(i+1)+i d。角 ∠A_iB_iA_{i+1} 是从射线 B_iA_{i+1} 旋转到射线 B_iA_i 的角，所以 ∠A_iB_iA_{i+1}=arg(z_i/w_i)。因此前 N 项和等于乘积的辐角：S_N=arg product_{i=1}^N ((i-1)+i d)/((i+1)+i d)。该乘积望远镜相消：product_{i=1}^N ((i-1)+i d)/((i+1)+i d)= [i d(1+i d)]/[(N+i d)(N+1+i d)]。当 N 趋于无穷时，分母两个因子的辐角都趋于 0，因此极限辐角为 arg(i d)+arg(1+i d)=π/2+tan^{-1}(d)。因为 d>0，有 tan^{-1}(d)+tan^{-1}(1/d)=π/2，所以总和为 π-tan^{-1}(1/d)。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This method packages the angles as arguments of complex-number ratios and obtains cancellation through a finite product, rather than directly writing and summing arctangent differences term by term. It is algebraic/rotational rather than purely angle-telescoping.
planner_metadata.image_role: The image shows the rays from each B_i to A_i and A_{i+1}, making it natural to interpret each desired angle as a rotation between two vectors. It also visually supports the coordinate orientation with the top and bottom parallel lines and A1 vertically above B1.
planner_metadata.text_role: The text provides the numerical increments along the two parallel lines, the common perpendicular distance d, and the fact that the A and B sequences proceed in the same direction, which determine the vector components used in the complex numbers.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the fact that the argument of a quotient of complex numbers equals the angle between the corresponding vectors, that sums of arguments equal arguments of products, telescoping cancellation in products, and the arctangent reciprocal identity for positive d.

raw_record.original_question: Two parallel lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ lie on a plane, distance $d$ apart. On $\ell_1$ there are an infinite number of points $A_1, A_2, A_3, ...$ , in that order, with $A_nA_{n+1} = 2$ for all $n$. On $\ell_2$ there are an infinite number of points $B_1, B_2, B_3,...$ , in that order and in the same direction, satisfying $B_nB_{n+1} = 1$ for all $n$. Given that $A_1B_1$ is perpendicular to both $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$, express the sum $\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \angle A_iB_iA_{i+1}$ in terms of $d$.\n<image1>
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure has two horizontal parallel straight lines; the upper straight line is \(\ell_1\), and the lower straight line is \(\ell_2\). Points \(A_1,A_2,A_3,\ldots\) are on the upper straight line, and points \(B_1,B_2,B_3,\ldots\) are on the lower straight line. In the figure, \(A_1\) is directly above \(B_1\), and \(A_1B_1\) is perpendicular to the two parallel lines. Each marked angle is located at \(B_i\), formed by the rays \(B_iA_i\) and \(B_iA_{i+1}\).

Establish a coordinate system according to the figure: let the lower straight line be the \(x\)-axis, and take \(B_1=(0,0)\). Since \(B_nB_{n+1}=1\), \(B_i=(i-1,0)\). The distance between the two lines is \(d\), and \(A_1\) is directly above \(B_1\), so \(A_1=(0,d)\). Also, since \(A_nA_{n+1}=2\), \(A_i=(2(i-1),d)\).

Viewed from \(B_i=(i-1,0)\), \(\overrightarrow{B_iA_i}=(i-1,d)\), and \(\overrightarrow{B_iA_{i+1}}=(i+1,d)\). Let \(f(k)=\arctan(d/k)\), and define \(f(0)=\pi/2\). Then the angle that ray \(B_iA_i\) makes with the positive horizontal direction is \(f(i-1)\), and the angle that ray \(B_iA_{i+1}\) makes with the positive horizontal direction is \(f(i+1)\). Therefore
\[
\angle A_iB_iA_{i+1}=f(i-1)-f(i+1).
\]

Summing the first \(N\) terms:
\[
\sum_{i=1}^N \angle A_iB_iA_{i+1}
=\sum_{i=1}^N [f(i-1)-f(i+1)]
=f(0)+f(1)-f(N)-f(N+1).
\]
When \(N\to\infty\), \(f(N),f(N+1)\to 0\), so the total sum is
\[
f(0)+f(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan(d).
\]
Since \(d>0\), there is
\[
\arctan(d)+\arctan(1/d)=\frac{\pi}{2},
\]
so
\[
\frac{\pi}{2}+\arctan(d)=\pi-\arctan(1/d).
\]
Therefore the desired sum is \(\pi-\tan^{-1}(1/d)\).
